result.title: Local Indices Are Not Enough: Synchrony and Global Information in Bandit Algorithms
result.summary: Standard index-based stochastic bandit algorithms such as KL-UCB and Thompson Sampling achieve optimal $O(\log T)$ regret over a horizon $T$. The former uses the global timestep to construct each arm's index, while the latter samples each arm's belief distribution at every timestep. The necessity of global information and synchronous index updates for achieving optimal regret has not been examined yet. In this paper, we investigate the fundamental limits of asynchronous local index algorithms---those that recalculate an arm's index only upon pulling it, using solely that arm's own reward history and a local randomness budget. We prove that no such algorithm can achieve $O(\log T)$ regret across all bandit instances. We then analyse the functional equations arising from asynchronous updates, and show that the achievable regret lies in a sub-polynomial, super-polylogarithmic regime. We propose an asynchronous local index policy whose regret upper bound also lies in this regime. Turning to synchronous local algorithms, which sample every arm's index at all timesteps as in Thompson Sampling, we show that a locally determined randomness budget per arm suffices to retain $O(\log T)$ regret, demonstrating that synchrony, albeit with some randomness, is essential to the optimality of Thompson Sampling.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究仅依赖单臂自身奖励历史、仅在拉取时更新的异步局部索引 bandit 算法的极限，证明此类算法无法达到 O(log T) 遗憾并刻画出次多项式、超多对数区间，同时证明同步采样配合局部随机性预算即可保持最优遗憾。
AI.relevance_reason: 其关于「局部信息加异步更新」不足以最优、而全局信息与同步计算具有必要性的结论，可能为核查 LVR 中每步 latent 状态更新是否需整合全局证据、以及随机性或计算预算如何影响决策质量提供概念参照。
